title: Comparison-Free Bit-Stream Generation for Cost-Efficient Unary Computing
problem: Converting binary radix data to unary representation via comparator-based generators incurs high area and power cost, especially as input count and precision increase.
motivation: Unary computing offers simplicity and noise tolerance advantages, but the conversion bottleneck limits practical adoption in hardware designs.
method: Binary numbers are converted to unary representation—expressing a value N as N ones in a sequence—traditionally using comparison circuits (comparators) that check if one number is larger than another. These circuits consume significant power and chip space, especially as input size increases. This design eliminates comparators entirely and instead uses alternative conversion logic to accomplish the same transformation. It provides three implementations: a serial approach that processes one value at a time (simpler, slower), and two parallel approaches (faster) that either compute the exact result or approximate it to reduce costs further.
key_novelty: A binary-to-unary conversion method that eliminates expensive comparison circuits (comparators) required by traditional approaches, removing their power and area overhead.
contributions: Reduced hardware area vs comparator-based converters
Two parallel generator variants (exact and approximate) for different use cases
limitations: Not discussed; limited details on area/power quantification.
primary_theme: Comparison-free unary number generation for efficient data conversion
